episodes.214810: A complex of showers and isolated thunderstorms tracked across western Pennsylvania during the early morning hours and continued to move eastward across central Pennsylvania during the late morning hours. As this complex moved eastward, surface heating ahead of the complex along with increasing moisture and shear allowed for more cohesive development into a line of strong-to-severe thunderstorms as it moved into York and Lancaster Counties. This produced multiple instances of tree damage across Lancaster County with an isolated instance of tree damage in York County. Heavy rainfall later in the evening across northwestern Pennsylvania also brought an isolated instance of flash flooding to Warren County.
episodes.214836: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front moving southeast through the region.
episodes.214847: A few severe thunderstorms developed along a moisture gradient in central Virginia, producing localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.214925: A thunderstorm formed over northern Shelby County and moved northward along I-65 through Jefferson County along an outflow boundary. Several instances of wind damage were reported, mainly in the form of downed trees and specifically in Vestavia Hills, Crestline, Crestwood, and Fultondale. A measured gust of 52 mph occurred at Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport. In addition, very heavy rainfall resulted in instances of roadway flooding as well as Valley Creek quickly rising into minor flood stage.
episodes.214962: An active summertime pattern continued for Middle Tennessee on August 8, 2026, as numerous thunderstorms developed over the area through the late evening hours. These thunderstorms produced very heavy rain, especially in the Williamson County area. Numerous roadways were reported and impassable with home evacuations and water rescues reported in the Franklin area.
episodes.215360: During the early to mid-afternoon hours, scattered thunderstorms developed across the Mogollon Rim and White Mountains, fueled by MLCAPE values around 1,000 J/kg. Steered by 15���20 kt easterly mid-level flow, these storms tracked westward into Gila County, while additional convective development occurred farther south through Pinal and Pima Counties. By early evening, outflows from these initial storm complexes triggered additional storm complexes across the lower deserts of south-central Arizona. One complex moved across western Pinal County into southwestern Maricopa County, producing localized flash flooding and strong winds. A more impactful storm complex developed over the Phoenix metropolitan area, particularly affecting West Valley communities including Glendale, Tolleson, Avondale, Goodyear, Litchfield Park, and Buckeye. This complex generated damaging wind gusts exceeding 70���80 mph, as sampled by the Phoenix Terminal Doppler Radar and verified by ground-truth observations. Reports from social media and local television news outlets indicated widespread wind damage along the storm's path. Numerous very large trees were uprooted or snapped, and heavy infrastructure damage occurred as multiple power poles were snapped or downed. Utility updates from Salt River Project (SRP) and Arizona Public Service (APS) indicated that more than 50,000 customers lost power at the peak of the storm. Structural damage was also widespread across the affected areas, including destroyed carports, blown-in garage doors, and roof parts blown off. The most severe structural impact was observed in Avondale, where extreme winds lifted and rolled several massive metal construction pipes���each weighing at least 1,000 lbs���into an adjacent neighborhood, causing extensive property damage. A weather balloon sounding launched three hours prior to storm initiation measured DCAPE values near 2,000 J/kg, placing it above the 90th percentile for the Phoenix sounding climatology and serving as the primary factor for the destructive wind gusts.
episodes.216032: A hot and humid air mass combined with strong northwest winds aloft, to bring a bout of severe storms to eastern Iowa August 7th. Several severe thunderstorms moved across eastern IA between 4pm and 10pm August 7th. Significant wind damage was surveyed in Buchanan and Linn counties with damage to crops, trees, power lines, farm buildings, and damage to siding on homes. The town of Prairieburg and rural portions of Buchanan county received the most extensive damage. In addition, three tornadoes were confirmed near Fairbank, Prairieburg and Rubio.
episodes.216163: During the mid-afternoon hours of August 9, a line of thunderstorms raced across southern Lake Michigan. As the line moved onshore, at least one report of thunderstorm wind damage was received in southwest Michigan. Later, the line of storms intensified to the southeast, producing additional wind damage over northern Indiana.
episodes.216164: During the mid-afternoon hours of August 9, a line of thunderstorms raced across southern Lake Michigan. As the line moved onshore the line continued to strengthen on its southeast flank. This resulted in numerous reports of thunderstorm wind damage over northern Indiana and northwest Ohio, primarily damage to trees.
episodes.216165: During the mid-afternoon hours of August 9, a line of thunderstorms raced across southern Lake Michigan. As the line moved onshore the line continued to strengthen on its southeast flank. This resulted in numerous reports of thunderstorm wind damage over northern Indiana and northwest Ohio, primarily damage to trees.
episodes.216234: Primarily diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms continued to impact the area from August 7th to the 9th under the guise of a front approaching from the northwest and then stalling across Ohio and Pennsylvania. This resulted in the daily formation of afternoon showers and thunderstorms, which produced damaging winds that brought down trees and power lines across southeast Ohio. Given saturated ground from previous rounds of rain already that month, one to three inches of rain produced by heavy downpours in these storms was enough to cause flash flooding on several roads in Meigs County.
episodes.216235: The active weather pattern that began the month of August continued to roll on into the 7th and 8th across West Virginia. This was due to a frontal boundary approaching from the northwest that then stalled across Ohio and Pennsylvania. This primed the atmosphere with ample moisture and unseasonably hot temperatures to help spawn the daily formation of afternoon showers and thunderstorms across the state. Scattered convection that developed both on the 7th and 8th of August inflicted downed trees and power lines across of variety of locations in West Virginia due to the damaging winds associated with the storms. Given the saturated ground from previous rounds of rain, one to three inches of rain produced by heavy downpours in these storms was also enough to cause flash flooding on several roads in West Virginia. Activity remained strongly connected to the warm temperature spread, with the loss of daytime heating at sunset causing their demise each evening.
episodes.216299: Severe thunderstorms moved across western Nebraska where Severe Thunderstorm Watch 549 was in place through midnight. Strong wind gusts were observed with these storms, as well as heavy rain. For Wyoming, a group of strong, gusty showers produced severe wind gusts along I-80.
episodes.216407: A line of severe thunderstorms moved across northeast Illinois from late morning through mid afternoon on August 9th producing scattered wind damage and localized flooding. Additional severe thunderstorms developed during the evening of August 9th across north central Illinois and moved southeast into east central Illinois by early morning on August 10th. This second round of thunderstorms produced wind damage and four tornadoes.
episodes.216408: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across far northwest Indiana during the afternoon of August 9th producing isolated wind damage and localized flooding.
episodes.216409: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across all of southern Lake Michigan during the early and mid afternoon of August 9th.
episodes.216432: A mid-level wave swept across the northern plains early Sunday morning of August 9th. A north-south oriented moisture gradient coincided with an area of surface convergence near the IA border which then extended up into southern MN. Most cells were sub-severe, however, one cell moving along the I-90 corridor produced quarter size hail 3 miles SSW of the Fairmont Municipal Airport.
episodes.216433: A mid-level wave swept across the Dakotas Saturday evening of August 8th. A weak isolated supercell developed over eastern South Dakota. This cell eventually strengthened and made its way into southwestern MN and produced nickel size hail in eastern Watonwan County just east of Lewisville.
episodes.216485: Isolated to scattered storms developed across the Piedmont and Sandhills of central North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A few reports of flooding and damaging winds were observed across Johnston, Moore, and Guilford Counties.
episodes.216687: More afternoon monsoon thunderstorms led to some severe weather and flash flooding from heavy rain.
episodes.216824: A cluster of storms moved across north central South Dakota during the late evening and early morning hours of August 8th/9th. Hail ranged from as large 1 to 1.5 inches in diameter, with crop damage noted by a trained spotter 3 miles northeast of Mound City (Campbell county).
episodes.216870: Two back-to-back tropical waves between August 9 and 11 produced thunderstorms across Puerto Rico. These led to flooding, mudslides, and wind gust damage.
episodes.216975: A couple rounds of thunderstorms in West Michigan produced isolated severe wind gusts during the afternoon of August 9, 2026, and later that night.
episodes.217355: On August 8th, 2026, a cold front approached from the northwest and slowly passed through the region. Ahead of the front, MLCAPE values exceeded 2000 J/kg, DCAPE of around 1200 J/kg, and low level lapse rates were ranging from 7-8 C/km. Though, shear in the environment was on the low end around 20-25 knots of bulk shear, and with the approaching front, it provided enough lift for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop.
episodes.217448: After a morning round of storms on August 8th, a lull in activity allowed for the development of an unstable atmosphere ahead of an afternoon shortwave. 1500-2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, along with around 1000 J/kg of downdraft CAPE, provided the ingredients for some isolated damaging wind gusts as scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms moved across the region.
episodes.217459: After a morning round of storms on August 8th, a lull in activity allowed for the development of an unstable atmosphere ahead of an afternoon shortwave. 1500-2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, along with around 1000 J/kg of downdraft CAPE, provided the ingredients for some isolated damaging wind gusts as scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms moved across the region.
episodes.217606: A couple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms in the vicinity of a stationary front produced large hail, damaging winds, and flooding in southern WI.
episodes.217677: During the peak heating hours of the day, PWATs began to surge to around 1.9-2.1 in combination with ample instability of around 2500+ J/kg of SBCAPE and weak shear.  Robust convection dipped into this instability to create swaths of damaging winds across areas mainly south of I-40. Convection began to dissipate around sunset as a shortwave translated east.
episodes.217707: Common daytime heating and sea breeze influences resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, as well as isolated strong to severe storms. Precipitable water values around 2.2+ inches and slow storm motion also resulted in multiple instances of very heavy rainfall and localized flooding.
episodes.217914: Concentrated warm air advection spurred a few thunderstorms in an environment with 2000-3000 J/kg elevated instability with marginally sufficient shear. Isolated rotating storms produced very large hail, with stones ejected from the stronger portions of the storm.
episodes.217947: High pressure centered across the Atlantic led to a typical summertime environment with general thunderstorms developing during afternoon hours across Southeast South Carolina.
episodes.217956: During the early morning hours of August 9th, storms brought strong wind gusts to portions of NW Missouri.
episodes.217958: Between August 7 and 9, a weakness emerged along the eastern periphery of a prominent mid-level ridge centered over New Mexico. This atmospheric feature prompted the formation of isolated to scattered thunderstorms across North Texas. A select number of these storms produced localized wind damage and small hail.
episodes.218007: Another day characterized by supportive instability and high precipitable water across the atmosphere led to scattered thunderstorms that produced high rain rates and heavy rainfall along with an isolated wet microburst.
episodes.218182: Isolated supercells developed during the afternoon and evening in south central North Dakota in an environment with marginal elevated instability. There was one report of severe hail in Emmons County, which was quarter sized hail near Strasburg.
episodes.218218: A surge of monsoon moisture brought thunderstorms to Clark County in southern Nevada.
episodes.218220: A surge of monsoon moisture brought thunderstorms to Mohave County in northwestern Arizona.
episodes.218224: A surge of monsoon moisture brought thunderstorms to southeastern California.
episodes.218274: An isolated severe thunderstorm wind event occurred across Kearny County where multiple severe wind gusts were measured with tree damage as well.
episodes.218294: A cold front across northern Kansas initiated thunderstorms in a very hot and dry airmass, leading to a few severe wind gusts in Kearny County.
episodes.218499: A broad area of thunderstorm activity developed during the afternoon of Saturday August 8th.  The region was under deep well mixed conditions with PWAT values greater than 1.6 that allowed for high efficiency precipitation processes.  In addition, strong surface heating created instability and energy.  The final ingredient was a weak mid-level disturbance that tracked across the region.  This allowed multi-cell thunderstorm activity to develop across the state during the afternoon hours.
episodes.218586: After a few days of decreased monsoon activity, thunderstorms increased in coverage to Santa Cruz and Pima Counties. Thunderstorms downed power poles and lines in Rio Rico and caused a power outage to 900 customers. Additionally, there was locally heavy rainfall from thunderstorms that caused rocks and debris to fall on Pendleton between Rio Rico Drive and Oceano Rd. A thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph was recorded in Tucson with no additional damage. A funnel cloud was reported on the SE side of Tucson.
